panels.title: Caption Lab — live CPU captioning and observability

options.content: **Refresh: 5 seconds.** Read from health to workload, latency and Ubuntu VM resources. Exporter UP means metrics are reachable; model READY means weights are loaded. The plots below use **Time (browser-local timezone) on the x-axis** and explicitly labeled **linear y-axes**. All values come from actual application/exporter observations.

panels.title: Application exporter
panels.description: Current status: 1 = ready/reachable; 0 = unavailable. A reachable exporter alone does not prove inference works.

panels.title: Caption model ready
panels.description: Current status: 1 = ready/reachable; 0 = unavailable. A reachable exporter alone does not prove inference works.

panels.title: Ubuntu node exporter
panels.description: Current status: 1 = ready/reachable; 0 = unavailable. A reachable exporter alone does not prove inference works.

panels.title: Active bulk jobs
panels.description: Current accepted bulk jobs, including work waiting for the CPU lock. Zero means no bulk job is in progress.

options.content:
Left: successful images per second by mode. Right: accepted jobs in progress, including CPU wait. Bulk activity should align with throughput and resource changes.

**X-axis: Time (browser-local timezone). Y-axes: linear; units on each plot.**

panels.title: Successful images • per mode
panels.description: Images completed per second over one minute. AI prompt: sum the rate of successful image counters separately for Single and Bulk; preserve mode comparison.

panels.title: Accepted jobs in progress
panels.description: Concurrent jobs may wait for one shared CPU model. Compare bulk activity with the resource panels on the same time axis.

panels.title: Inference time versus user-visible image time

options.content:
Left: mean and estimated p95 for model.generate only. Right: per-image mean including decode and queue delay. Missing observations produce gaps, not zero-second inference.

**X-axis: Time (browser-local timezone). Y-axes: linear; units on each plot.**

panels.title: Model inference • mean and p95
panels.description: Wall time in model.generate only. AI prompt: weighted mean = sum(rate(duration_sum))/sum(rate(duration_count)); approximate p95 = histogram_quantile over summed buckets. No observations gives a gap, not zero latency.

panels.title: Per-image latency • decode + queue + inference
panels.description: AI prompt: calculate weighted per-mode mean image latency from histogram sums and counts. Queue delay is included here, unlike model inference.

options.content:
Left: Summary mean for an entire job; a ZIP is one job. Right: image success/error totals since backend start. Counters reset on restart.

**X-axis: Time (browser-local timezone). Y-axes: linear; units on each plot.**

panels.title: Whole-job duration • Summary
panels.description: AI prompt: mean full-job duration = Summary sum rate divided by Summary observation count rate, per mode. Bulk includes all images, so it should usually exceed Single. Python Summary has _sum and _count, not built-in quantiles.

panels.title: Images attempted since backend start
panels.description: AI prompt: sum image counters by mode and success/error outcome. These totals reset when the backend restarts; status is also written in the result CSV.

panels.title: Correlate bulk uploads with Ubuntu VM resources

options.content:
Left: VM CPU averaged over cores. Right: VM memory using MemAvailable. Orange bars on each right axis show bulk jobs. These measure Ubuntu, not the Mac host.

**X-axis: Time (browser-local timezone). Y-axes: linear; units on each plot.**

panels.title: Ubuntu VM CPU • correlate with bulk
panels.description: AI prompt: VM CPU percent = 100*(1-mean(rate(idle CPU seconds[1m]))) over VM cores. Bulk line uses the right axis. These are Ubuntu guest metrics, not Mac host metrics.

panels.title: Ubuntu VM memory • correlate with bulk
panels.description: AI prompt: used-memory percent = 100*(1-MemAvailable/MemTotal). Bulk jobs use the right axis. MemAvailable includes reclaimable memory; do not substitute MemFree.

options.content:
Left: Ubuntu root disk used percent. Right: backend RSS versus model weights; RSS includes runtime overhead. Streamlit memory is included only in VM-wide measurements.

**X-axis: Time (browser-local timezone). Y-axes: linear; units on each plot.**

panels.title: Ubuntu root filesystem • used space
panels.description: AI prompt: root filesystem used percent = 100*(1-avail/size), select mountpoint=/ and exclude tmpfs/overlay. This measures the guest filesystem, not the Mac disk.

panels.title: Inference-process RAM and model weights
panels.description: Model weights are parameter/buffer storage only; RSS also includes Python, temporary tensors and decoded inputs. These are bytes, not VM-wide RAM.

options.content:
Left: successful, partial and failed completed jobs. Right: image totals by short actual session ID. Use the table labels to distinguish sessions; prefixes can collide and are not user counts.

**X-axis: Time (browser-local timezone). Y-axes: linear; units on each plot.**

panels.title: Jobs completed by outcome
panels.description: AI prompt: sum completed job counters for success/partial/error separately. Partial means some ZIP members failed. Counters reset on backend restart.

panels.title: Client sessions • image activity
panels.description: AI prompt: show successful image counts by the first 12 safe characters of the actual browser session ID. Session prefixes are not unique people and can collide. For a small demo only; avoid unbounded labels in production.

options.content:
Left: 100% CPU means one full core, so this can exceed 100%. Right: rejected request count; corrupt images inside accepted ZIPs appear in image errors instead.

**X-axis: Time (browser-local timezone). Y-axes: linear; units on each plot.**

panels.title: Inference-process CPU
panels.description: 100% equals one fully used CPU core; this can exceed 100% on multiple cores. VM CPU above is normalized across all VM cores.

panels.title: Rejected uploads
panels.description: Rejected oversized or malformed uploads. Corrupt images inside accepted jobs are counted in image errors instead. Rejections do not become accepted jobs.

options.content:
Left: accepted uploaded bytes per second, including compressed ZIP size. Right: firing alert count. Check the local receiver for actual alert delivery.

**X-axis: Time (browser-local timezone). Y-axes: linear; units on each plot.**

panels.title: Uploaded input bytes • rate
panels.description: AI prompt: show rate of accepted uploaded-byte counters separately by mode. This is application input volume, not operating-system network traffic.

panels.title: Prometheus firing alerts
panels.description: Number of firing alert series. Check Prometheus Alerts, Alertmanager and the local receiver for details; pending conditions are excluded.

options.content:
Left: encoded bytes per attempted image, including corrupt entries. Right: Unicode characters per successful caption, including spaces. Caption length is not an accuracy metric.

**X-axis: Time (browser-local timezone). Y-axes: linear; units on each plot.**

panels.title: Encoded image size • Summary mean
panels.description: AI prompt: weighted mean bytes per attempted image = sum(rate(caption_image_upload_bytes_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(caption_image_upload_bytes_count[5m])), separately by mode. Includes corrupt image entries; excludes ZIP compression overhead.

panels.title: Generated caption length • Summary mean
panels.description: AI prompt: weighted mean Unicode characters per successful caption = sum(rate(caption_length_characters_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(caption_length_characters_count[5m])), separately by mode. Includes spaces, excludes failed captions; length is not a quality score.
